alerts.title: AKI likely pre-renal from gastroenteritis, not TDF toxicity
alerts.message: Guidelines note that intercurrent illnesses with dehydration or sepsis may cause renal deterioration in patients on TDF, requiring creatinine checking during hospital admissions. This patient has severe gastroenteritis with dehydration (BP 90/60, dry mucous membranes, reduced skin turgor), two affected family members suggesting infectious gastroenteritis, and a urea-to-creatinine ratio of 24:1 favouring pre-renal AKI. Urinalysis shows no protein or glucose, which argues against TDF-induced tubular toxicity. Baseline creatinine was normal (0.9) one year ago. The acute presentation over 5 days with hypovolaemia strongly supports pre-renal AKI rather than chronic TDF nephrotoxicity. Permanent discontinuation of TDF may be unnecessary if renal function recovers with fluid resuscitation.

evidence.recommended_action: Resuscitate with IV fluids and recheck creatinine before deciding on permanent TDF discontinuation. If renal function recovers, TDF may be continued with ongoing monitoring.

alerts.title: DTG creatinine rise algorithm does not apply to acute AKI
alerts.message: Guidelines describe a DTG-related creatinine rise algorithm for small, stable increases (<30 µmol/L) occurring within the first month of DTG initiation. This patient's creatinine rose from 0.9 to 2.4 mg/dL (increase ~133 µmol/L) after 2 years on DTG, which is far outside the DTG-related pattern. The magnitude and acuity are inconsistent with DTG-related creatinine elevation. This acute rise should be attributed to the gastroenteritis episode and managed with fluid resuscitation rather than DTG adjustment.

evidence.recommended_action: Do not attribute this acute creatinine rise to DTG. Focus on treating the underlying gastroenteritis and dehydration, then reassess renal function before considering regimen changes.

alerts.title: If TDF stopped, guideline-recommended alternative is ABC+3TC+DTG
alerts.message: Guidelines state that if renal impairment develops due to TDF, the recommended alternative regimen is ABC + 3TC + DTG. If the clinician decides to permanently discontinue TDF after this AKI episode, this specific switch should be used. However, given the pre-renal presentation, temporary TDF continuation with close monitoring during recovery may be more appropriate than permanent discontinuation.

evidence.recommended_action: If TDF is permanently discontinued, switch to ABC + 3TC + DTG as per guideline. Consider temporary hold with reassessment after resuscitation instead.
